sq.q: What is the purpose of importing packages in Java?
answer: Importing packages allows access to classes, interfaces, and methods defined in another package. This improves code reusability, supports modular design, and makes programs more organized.

sq.q: Write the steps and code snippet to create a user-defined package named shapes containing a class Circle.
answer: Step 1: Create the class inside the package // File: shapes/Circle.java package shapes; public class Circle { public void draw() { System.out.println("Drawing a circle"); } } Step 2: Import and use the package // File: Main.java import shapes.Circle; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Circle c = new Circle(); c.draw(); } } Step 3: Compile with folder structure javac shapes/Circle.java javac -cp . Main.java

lq.q: You are building a Java-based library management system. You want to organize your project into different functional units: books, users, and transactions. Explain how you can use user-defined packages to structure your codebase. Illustrate with Java code how to define and import classes from these packages. What are the benefits of this modular approach?
answer: Folder Structure: library/ ??? books/ ? ??? Book.java ??? users/ ? ??? User.java ??? transactions/ ? ??? Transaction.java ??? Main.java Sample Code: books/Book.java package books; public class Book { public void displayBook() { System.out.println("Displaying book info..."); } } users/User.java package users; public class User { public void displayUser() { System.out.println("Displaying user info..."); } } transactions/Transaction.java package transactions; public class Transaction { public void displayTransaction() { System.out.println("Displaying transaction info..."); } } Main.java import books.Book; import users.User; import transactions.Transaction; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { Book b = new Book(); User u = new User(); Transaction t = new Transaction(); b.displayBook(); u.displayUser(); t.displayTransaction(); } } Benefits of This Modular Approach: Better organization of code by separating concerns Encourages code reusability across projects Supports team collaboration, as different teams can work on separate packages Makes maintenance and scaling easier
